- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for 2–3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5–10% gap), apply a “sentiment-weighted decay” — reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day based on sentiment magnitude.
- If sentiment is neutral (±0.33) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
